Subject: Cascade Legal Rights Project response and clinic update

We’re writing on behalf of Cascade Legal Rights Project in response to the concerns raised here. We understand why receiving a lawyer’s letter shortly after asking for help would be frightening. People should feel able to seek information about their housing without worrying that doing so will put them at risk.

Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing clinic attendees’ information to landlords or their attorneys. Clinic sign-in records are kept internally in locked storage.

Eviction filings in magistrate court are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for the letters described here, though we can’t determine the source of any particular letter from this discussion. We won’t discuss anyone’s individual circumstances on the board.

The free tenant rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library meeting room is closed for repairs, so the clinic has moved to the Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible.

Everyone is still welcome, and no appointment is needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

If you have questions about the clinic or our handling of information, please email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. Please don’t post personal details or case information here.

Cascade Legal Rights Project
